- Merge all into a single test file ParseErrorTest.java, wrapped with ###Test START## and ###Test END##.

Class ParseError has:

- public String getErrorMessage()
- public int getPosition()
- public String toString() (overrides Object's toString, also public)

Constructors are package-private, not public. But tests can instantiate using those constructors because test class is in same package or we can use reflection. Usually test class can be placed in same package (org.jsoup.parser) to access package-private constructors. We'll assume same package.

Edge cases: null errorMsg? Constructors accept String errorMsg directly; can pass null. Also errorFormat with args causing NullPointerException? String.format with null format leads to NullPointerException. Also passing null args? It accepts varargs; null as args array leads to NPE? Actually String.format(null, args) throws NPE. Also passing format string with mismatched placeholders may cause IllegalFormatException.

Also position negative? No validation; test that negative pos is stored.

Also test toString formatting.

We need basic tests: test getErrorMessage returns what is set, test getPosition returns set, test toString returns "pos: msg".

Edge cases: null message, null format (expect NPE), mismatched format (IllegalFormatException), negative position.

Also test that errorFormat with args correctly formats.

Write JUnit 4 tests using @Test annotation, expected exceptions.

Set package to org.jsoup.parser.

Add imports: org.junit.Test, static org.junit.Assert.*.

Write test methods naming.
